title: Batch Pipeline Incident Post-mortem
subtitle: What failed during the nightly batch outage, how it was detected, and what changes so it does not repeat.
source: Illustrative timeline and figures. Not a real incident.

summary.verdict: A schema change shipped without a contract check broke the nightly batch for 6 hours. No data was lost; downstream reports were late.
text: Detection took 95 minutes because the alert watched job exit codes rather than output row counts. Recovery was a rerun after a revert.

table.caption: Table 1. Key events, UTC (Illustrative).
rows: Nightly batch starts with the new schema.
Transform step writes empty partitions; exit code stays 0.

blocks.p: The upstream team renamed a column. The transform step read the old name, produced nulls and filtered them out as invalid, so the job succeeded with empty output.

code.caption: Transform filter that hid the failure (Illustrative).
code.text: df = df.filter(col("order_total").isNotNull())  # renamed upstream to total_amount

callout.title: Contributing factor
callout.text: The runbook had no step to compare output row counts with the previous run.

findings.title: No schema contract between producer and consumer
findings.text: A breaking rename reached production without any automated check.
findings.evidence: The change passed code review and unit tests; none covered the column contract.
findings.recommendation: Add a contract test to the producer pipeline.

findings.title: Alerting ignores output volume
findings.text: The job succeeded with zero rows, and no alert fired.
findings.recommendation: Alert when row count drops more than 30% against the 7-day median.

findings.title: Rollback was manual but fast
findings.text: The revert took 35 minutes once the cause was known.
findings.evidence: Revert merged at 03:10 and verified at 03:45.

recommendations.title: Contract test for the orders feed
Add output comparison to the runbook
